environment.execution: WebGPU in one persistent dedicated worker

input.description: Same fixed grayscale PNG as webgpu-2026-10-27.json; no resizing in browser

notes: CPU values are synchronous host wall time, not CPU cycle counters. GPU timestamps use their own clock and overlap host/wait times; do not add them.
The frame mode keeps the normal single compute pass and adds one outer GPU timestamp window. Its GPU interval is the minimally instrumented reference.
Kernel timing forces per-kernel pass boundaries and extra submissions. Its GPU window includes profiler-induced idle gaps; it is not production GPU execution cost.
Missing GPU durations stay null, not zero. The measured kernel sum is partial when coverage is incomplete. Summary fields are separate medians and are not additive.
API calls below the measured ~0.1 ms CPU clock quantum may show zero. API sync time excludes async wait; async settled latency sums overlap and are not total elapsed readback time.
Ordinary warmed frames create no GPU buffers, shader modules or compute pipelines. The 12-warmup historical comparison was an early warm-up snapshot, not a steady-state CPU/GPU comparison.
Default application builds do not enable profiling; shader math, detector parameters and normal batching are unchanged.

conclusion: The historical 31 ms submit phase is host-side queue/runtime work, not GPU shader duration. With longer warm-up baseline p50 is 24.6 ms initially and 24.7 ms in the final control; submit wall time is ~11.8 ms, the frame GPU interval ~5.44 ms, readback/wait ~8.5 ms. This profile does not identify the exact host runtime function behind the residual cost.
